Theme

Household, washing & chores · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

domestic adjective

of the home and family

also household, family (as adjective), home life, domestic affairs, household chores, domestic animals

classical

Cic. Fin. 2.77: aliam domesticam, aliam forēnsem
Tac. Dial. 34.1: domesticā disciplīnā

domesticus, domestica, domesticum

declension

of the house and household; family, private

Of the house itself (vestis domestica, clothes for wearing at home), but far more often of the family and its affairs: rēs domesticae ac familiārēs against public business, a family grief, home training; as a noun, domesticī, the members of a household (Lewis & Short). Household animals are avēs domesticae, poultry (Col.; M-O s.v. types: chicken: fowl); for the other sense, “not foreign”, see domestic (of one’s own country).

Other words

  • familiāris, familiāre — of the household or family; intimate, familiar

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.2: rēs domesticās ac familiārēs (Lewis & Short, s.v. domesticus)

    Of the familia, the household with its slaves and property: rēs familiāris is one’s estate. More often of persons, “intimate, familiar”, and as a noun a close friend (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • cum extrā rem pūblicam in domesticā rē atque vītā sedeātur, ambulētur, in convīviō quoque familiārī discumbātur

    when, away from public affairs, in home life and domestic matters, people sit, walk about, and recline at a family dinnerGell. 2.2.9

  • imbūtus jam domesticā disciplīnā, refertus honestīs studiīs dēdūcēbātur ā patre vel ā propinquīs ad eum ōrātōrem, quī prīncipem in cīvitāte locum obtinēbat

    already schooled at home and full of honourable studies, he was taken by his father or his relatives to the orator who held the first place in the cityTac. Dial. 34.1

See also domestic, formal, private, house, pet.

SourcesLewis & Short: domesticus · Lewis & Short: familiaris

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. types: chicken: fowl.
